description: Initialize the Cargo workspace and all seven member crates with placeholders, correct dependency direction, and a smoke test per crate (tasks.md P0.1, P0.2, and the Rust portion of P0.5). This establishes the offline-verifiable green baseline. Because the sandbox is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY (crates.io unreachable), the six library crates MUST be dependency-free so `cargo build/test/clippy` pass offline, and `tauri-app` (which needs the external `tauri` crate) is kept in workspace `members` for spec fidelity but excluded from `default-members`.
steps: Create hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml as a virtual workspace manifest. Set `resolver = "2"`. `members = ["crates/orchestrator-core", "crates/providers", "crates/mcp-client", "crates/routing", "crates/persistence", "crates/secrets", "crates/tauri-app"]`. Set `default-members` to the SIX library crates only (exclude crates/tauri-app) so a bare `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy` in the sandbox does not try to resolve the unreachable `tauri` crate. Add a `[workspace.package]` section with shared version = "0.1.0", edition = "2021", license. Add an explanatory comment above default-members noting why tauri-app is excluded from default-members (offline registry constraint) and that CI builds it explicitly.

Create the five simple library crates each with Cargo.toml (name, version.workspace/edition.workspace, empty [dependencies]) and src/lib.rs: crates/providers (with the src/ subtree files as empty placeholder modules per Section 3.2: contract.rs, registry.rs, capability.rs, adapters/{openai,lmstudio,azure_openai,anthropic,gemini,bedrock,generic_openai}.rs each containing only a `//! placeholder` doc comment; declare the module tree in lib.rs), crates/mcp-client (transport/{stdio,http_sse}.rs, session.rs, tools.rs placeholders declared in lib.rs), crates/routing (policy.rs, signals.rs, policies/{auto_default,manual_override,registry}.rs placeholders declared in lib.rs), crates/persistence (db.rs, repositories.rs, config.rs placeholders declared in lib.rs), crates/secrets (lib.rs only per Section 3.2). Each crate's lib.rs must include one trivial passing smoke test: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { #[test] fn smoke() { assert!(true); } }`. Keep every one of these crates dependency-free (no external crates).

Create crates/orchestrator-core with Cargo.toml that depends on the other five library crates via path dependencies (providers, mcp-client, routing, persistence, secrets) using `{ path = "../<crate>" }`. This establishes that orchestrator-core depends on the libs (Section 3.3 dependency direction). src/lib.rs declares modules session.rs, pipeline.rs, events.rs (empty placeholder doc comments) and includes a smoke test that references at least one item from each dependency crate to prove the wiring compiles (e.g. call a trivial `pub fn placeholder()` you add to each lib crate). Add a `pub fn placeholder()` (or a marker const) to each of the 5 lib crates so orchestrator-core can reference them in its smoke test, proving the dependency edges actually compile. Keep orchestrator-core otherwise dependency-free (only the 5 path deps).

Create crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml as a binary crate that depends (via path) on orchestrator-core and the library crates, plus the external `tauri`, `serde`, and `serde_json` crates (these will only resolve in CI where network exists). Add the tauri build-dependency `tauri-build`. Do NOT add tauri-app to default-members. Its source files (main.rs etc.) are created in FEAT-002; for this feature just create the Cargo.toml and a minimal src/main.rs stub so the manifest is valid, but understand it will not compile offline (that is expected and documented).

Ensure the crate dependency direction is correct and no library crate depends on tauri-app. orchestrator-core -> {providers, mcp-client, routing, persistence, secrets}; tauri-app -> {orchestrator-core + libs}; libs depend on nothing internal (except orchestrator-core's edges above).

Run `cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build` (bare, uses default-members) and confirm the six library crates compile offline. Run `cargo test` and confirm one smoke test per library crate passes. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (over default-members) and confirm no errors. Commit hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.lock (lockfile policy).
acceptance_criteria: `cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build` succeeds offline (builds the 6 default-member library crates without contacting any registry).
`cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo test` passes with at least one smoke test in each of the 6 library crates (orchestrator-core, providers, mcp-client, routing, persistence, secrets).
`cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` reports no errors over default-members.
orchestrator-core's Cargo.toml has path dependencies on all five other library crates and its smoke test references an item from each, proving the dependency edges compile.
No library crate depends on tauri-app; tauri-app is in `members` but not in `default-members`.
The directory tree under hybrid-orchestrator/crates/ matches architecture.md Section 3.2 exactly (all listed src files present as placeholders).
findings:
Created the Cargo workspace at hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml and all seven crates under hybrid-orchestrator/crates/. The src file tree reproduces architecture.md Section 3.2 exactly; every placeholder module is a file with a `//!` doc comment and is declared in its crate's lib.rs. The five leaf lib crates (providers, mcp-client, routing, persistence, secrets) are dependency-free and each exposes `pub fn placeholder()`. orchestrator-core has path dependencies on all five leaf crates, and its smoke test calls each crate's `placeholder()` to prove the dependency edges compile. tauri-app is a binary crate whose Cargo.toml depends (path) on orchestrator-core + the five libs plus external tauri/serde/serde_json and the tauri-build build-dependency; it has a minimal src/main.rs stub (full source deferred to FEAT-002).

DEVIATION (important): The briefing/steps asked to keep tauri-app in workspace `members` but exclude it from `default-members`, expecting bare cargo commands to stay green offline. In cargo 1.92 this does NOT work: cargo resolves the ENTIRE workspace dependency graph (all `members`, not just `default-members`) to build Cargo.lock. Because `tauri` is unreachable offline (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, crates.io returns 403), ANY cargo command (build/test/clippy/fmt/generate-lockfile), with or without --offline and with or without -p scoping, failed with 'failed to get serde as a dependency of tauri-app' / 'no matching package named tauri'. Verified this exhaustively. To satisfy the offline-green acceptance criteria that are actually verifiable in-sandbox, tauri-app is placed under `[workspace] exclude` instead of `members`. It remains present in the source tree for spec fidelity; CI (with network) generates a lockfile including tauri's deps and builds it via `cargo build -p tauri-app`, or re-adds it to `members` once that networked lockfile is committed. A detailed explanatory comment documents this in hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.toml and crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml. This means one acceptance criterion ('tauri-app is in members but not in default-members') is intentionally not met as literally worded, because it is unachievable offline; the intent (tauri-app excluded from the offline default build, kept for CI/spec) is preserved.

MINOR DEVIATION: The steps specified smoke tests of the form `assert!(true)`, but `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` rejects that via clippy::assertions_on_constants. Replaced each smoke-test body with a real call (`super::placeholder()` for the leaf crates; orchestrator-core already calls all five deps' placeholder()), which is meaningful, passes clippy under -D warnings, and still constitutes one passing smoke test per crate.

Added hybrid-orchestrator/.gitignore (ignores /target). Committed hybrid-orchestrator/Cargo.lock (6 offline crates).

VERIFICATION (all run from /projects/agent-harbor/hybrid-orchestrator, all PASS offline):
- `cargo build` -> Finished; compiles the 6 default (now sole) member lib crates, no registry contact.
- `cargo test` -> 6 smoke tests pass (1 per lib crate), all doc-tests 0/pass.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` -> Finished, no errors.
- `cargo fmt --check` -> clean (exit 0).
NOT verifiable in-sandbox (documented, not attempted as passing): `cargo build -p tauri-app` (needs tauri from crates.io), tauri dev/build (CLI absent + network + display), frontend npm/vitest (npm registry blocked). These are CI-gated and are later features.
